title: Universal first order thickenings and conormal sheaves under flat base change
statement: Let $h':W\to Y$ be a formally unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism], $g:X\to Y$ a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], and $Z=X\times_YW$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $h:Z\to X$ and $f:Z\to W$. Let $W\subset W'$ be a universal first order thickening of $W$ over $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i_W:W\to W'$ and structure morphism $W'\to Y$. Then: (1) $h$ is formally unramified; (2) the morphism $i_Z:=\mathrm{id}_X\times i_W:Z=X\times_YW\to Z':=X\times_YW'$ makes $Z\subset Z'$, with the projection $Z'\to X$, a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$; (3) with $f':Z'\to W'$ the projection, so that $f'\circ i_Z=i_W\circ f$, the morphism $f'$ is flat and the canonical map $f^*\mathcal C_{W/Y}\to\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ of conormal sheaves [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified], [def-pc-module-pullback], induced by $f'^\sharp$ (which maps $f'^{-1}$ of the ideal sheaf of $i_W$ into the ideal sheaf of $i_Z$, Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 01R4 [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial]), is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 04F8 (lemma-universal-thickening-fibre-product) and Lemma 04F9 (lemma-universal-thickening-fibre-product-flat); the conormal map is Morphisms, Lemma 01R4 (lemma-conormal-functorial), its bijectivity Morphisms, Lemma 0473 (lemma-conormal-functorial-flat)

proof.text: *(1) $h$ is formally unramified.* The pair of projections $(f,h)$ makes $Z$ a fibre product of $h'$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; exchanging the factors (the unique isomorphism $X\times_YW\cong W\times_YX$ compatible with the projections, from the universal property) identifies $h$ with the projection $W\times_YX\to X$, i.e. the base change of $h'$ along $g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-base-change] (applied to the formally unramified $h':W\to Y$ and $g:X\to Y$) this projection is formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]; and the defining lifting condition is unchanged under composing with an isomorphism over $X$ (lifts $a'$ correspond bijectively), so $h$ is formally unramified.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F8 (lemma-universal-thickening-fibre-product), first sentence, citing Lemma 02HB (lemma-base-change-formally-unramified)

proof.text: *$Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening over $X$.* Let $s:W'\to Y$ be the structure morphism, so $s\circ i_W=h'$, let $Z'=X\times_YW'$ be the fibre product of $g$ and $s$ with projections $p_X:Z'\to X$ and $f':Z'\to W'$, and $i_Z=\mathrm{id}_X\times_Yi_W$ the induced morphism [def-pc-fibre-product], so $p_X\circ i_Z=h$ and $f'\circ i_Z=i_W\circ f$. In the diagram with rows $Z\xrightarrow{f}W$, $Z'\xrightarrow{f'}W'$, $X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ and columns $i_Z,p_X$ resp. $i_W,s$, the lower square is cartesian (definition of $Z'$) and the outer rectangle ($Z\to W$, $Z\xrightarrow{p_X\circ i_Z=h}X$ over $Y$) is cartesian (definition of $Z$); by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian: $(Z,i_Z,f)$ is a fibre product of $f'$ and $i_W$. Since $W\subset W'$ is a first order thickening [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], [lem-weil-pbc-first-order-thickening-base-change] applied to $i=i_W$ and $p=f'$ shows that $i_Z$ is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z=\mathcal I_W\mathcal O_{Z'}$ has square zero. So $Z\subset Z'$ with $p_X:Z'\to X$, $p_X\circ i_Z=h$, is a first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$, and $(f,f'):(Z\subset Z')\to(W\subset W')$ is a morphism of thickenings. In Lean, the cartesian square gives the comparison isomorphism to the chosen pullback of the ambient second projection and i_W. Transport the closed immersion by composition with this isomorphism, and transport the square-zero kernel by Scheme.Hom.ker_comp_of_isIso.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F8: 'It is clear that X x_Y W' is a first order thickening', which is Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening)

proof.text: *(2) The universal property.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $X$, with closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ (square-zero ideal), structure morphism $b:T'\to X$, and $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$. Regard $T\subset T'$ as a first order thickening over $Y$ through $g\circ b$, and $f\circ a:T\to W$: then $h'\circ(f\circ a)=g\circ h\circ a=g\circ b\circ i_T$. By the universal property of $W'$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is exactly one $c:T'\to W'$ with $s\circ c=g\circ b$ and $c\circ i_T=i_W\circ f\circ a$. Existence: put $a'=(b,c):T'\to Z'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (defined as $g\circ b=s\circ c$); then $p_X\circ a'=b$, and $a'\circ i_T=i_Z\circ a$ because both have first component $b\circ i_T=h\circ a=p_X\circ i_Z\circ a$ and second component $c\circ i_T=i_W\circ f\circ a=f'\circ i_Z\circ a$ (step 2), and a morphism to $Z'$ is determined by its components. Uniqueness: if $a''$ satisfies $p_X\circ a''=b$ and $a''\circ i_T=i_Z\circ a$, then $c''=f'\circ a''$ satisfies $s\circ c''=g\circ p_X\circ a''=g\circ b$ and $c''\circ i_T=f'\circ i_Z\circ a=i_W\circ f\circ a$, so $c''=c$ by the uniqueness for $W'$, and $a''=(b,c)=a'$. Hence $Z\subset Z'$ with $p_X$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$. Moreover $f'$ is the morphism of universal thickenings of Stacks Lemma 04F7: it is the unique $c:Z'\to W'$ with $s\circ c=g\circ p_X$ and $c\circ i_Z=i_W\circ f$ (the case $T'=Z'$, $a=\mathrm{id}_Z$).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F8: 'It is straightforward to check that it has the universal property because W' has the universal property (by mapping properties of fibre products)'; Lemma 04F7 (lemma-universal-thickening-functorial) for the canonical morphism (f,f')

proof.text: *(3) $f'$ is flat.* $f':Z'=X\times_YW'\to W'$ is the projection of the fibre product of the flat morphism $g:X\to Y$ with $s:W'\to Y$, i.e. the base change of $g$ along $s$; by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F9 (lemma-universal-thickening-fibre-product-flat), first two sentences, citing Morphisms, Lemma 01U9 (morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat)

proof.text: Compute both conormal modules directly from the supplied universal thickenings using [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified] and [def-pc-module-pullback]: these definitions are the tensor pullbacks of the kernel ideals for i_W and i_Z. No choice of a further thickening or independence comparison is required. For the cartesian square constructed in step 2, the map specified in the statement is exactly the canonical map of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-flat-base-change] to that map and the flat ambient second projection from step 4. Its isomorphism conclusion proves the final clause.
